subject: Food Science
title: Starch and Thickening
description: A 60-second lesson on Starch and Thickening.

hook.text: A tablespoon of cornstarch can turn a cup of liquid into a thick sauce. The starch granules swell to 30 times their original size.

buildup.text: Starch granules absorb water when heated. At 60–80°C they swell and burst, releasing amylose chains that tangle together.

discovery.text: This process is called gelatinization. Different starches gelatinize at different temperatures.

twist.text: Overcooking breaks the long chains and the sauce thins again—called starch breakdown.

climax.text: Cornstarch makes clear sauces; flour makes opaque ones. Flour has protein (gluten) that scatters light.

punchline.text: Heat makes starch granules swell and burst—thickening liquid. Too much heat undoes it all.

quiz.question: Why does cornstarch produce clear sauces while flour makes opaque ones?
options: Cornstarch is pure starch—flour contains protein that scatters light
